books.section: Topic 3.10 Shaping the New Republic, G. The Struggle for Neutrality in the 1790s

source: original; stimulus quotes George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796, public domain.

stimulus.text: George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796: “It is our true policy to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.” Washington asked: “Why, by interweaving our destiny with that of any part of Europe, entangle our peace and prosperity in the toils of European ambition, rivalship, interest, humor, or caprice?” Washington also warned, in the most solemn manner, against “the baneful effects of the spirit of party generally,” saying it “serves always to distract the public councils and enfeeble the public administration.”
stimulus.source: George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796. Public domain.
stimulus.source_note: George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796. Public domain.

parts.prompt: Identify ONE warning Washington gives in the Farewell Address.
parts.modelAnswer: One warning is against permanent alliances with any foreign nation. Washington also warns against the spirit of party, which he says distracts public councils and weakens the administration.

scoring.criterion: Names one warning from the address, such as avoiding permanent alliances or guarding against the spirit of party.
scoring.notEarned: Naming a topic Washington discussed without stating the warning does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE reason Washington gives for avoiding permanent alliances.
parts.modelAnswer: Washington says permanent alliances would entangle American peace and prosperity in Europe’s ambition and rivalry, dragging the young nation into wars not its own. He warns against tying the nation’s fate to one side in Europe’s endless conflicts.

scoring.criterion: Explains one reason Washington gives for avoiding permanent alliances, such as entangling American peace and prosperity in Europe’s ambition and rivalry, or being dragged into Europe’s wars.
scoring.notEarned: Restating the warning without giving a reason does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way the Farewell Address reflects the political divisions of the 1790s.
parts.modelAnswer: The address reflects the split between Federalists, who leaned toward Britain, and Democratic-Republicans, who leaned toward France. Washington warned against both foreign attachments and party spirit because each side accused the other of serving a foreign power.

scoring.criterion: Explains one way the address reflects the divisions of the 1790s, such as the Federalist and Democratic-Republican split over France and Britain, or the way foreign attachments fed party hatred.
scoring.notEarned: Naming the parties without linking them to the address does not earn the point.
